title: Candidate first-week sensory onboard playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a practical, sensory-first playbook for a new hire's first 5 working days (week 1). The goal is to reduce cognitive friction, ensure consistent signals to candidates/hires, and give managers/buddies an actionable checklist that focuses on experience (not just access).

Audience:
- Hiring manager
- Onboarding buddy
- People Ops coordinator

High-level principles (why sensory-first):
- New hires remember rhythms and small details; controlling sensory inputs (timing of meetings, noise, tooling introductions) reduces overwhelm.
- Small rituals (intro coffee, 30-min demo) create measurable retention and confidence.
- Focus on 3 wins in week 1: access, context, one deploy/landmark task.

Prereqs (before day 0):
- Manager confirms start-of-day agenda + first-week 1:1 timeslot (calendar invite sent).
- IT: laptop imaged, headphones packaged, dongles tested. (Ticket: JIRA-IT-782)
- Security: account created, baseline training auto-enrolled.
- People Ops: welcome email + hardware checklist + buddy assigned.

Day-by-day sensory checklist (concise, useable):
- Day 0 (pre-start): welcome doc + heartbeat message from manager. Include short 2-min video intro or voice note.
- Day 1 AM (low sensory): 
  - 09:00 — Quiet welcome: 15m manager check-in (no slides). Purpose: human connection.
  - 09:30 — Systems walk: account checklist with IT buddy, shared screen.
  - 11:00 — Short team intro (20m): round-robin, 1 sentence each (no long slide decks).
  - 13:00 — Lunch: calendar reserved for lunch - "intro buddy lunch" (opt-in).
  - 15:00 — Workstation ergonomics quick check + keyboard shortcuts cheat-sheet.
- Day 2 (context building):
  - 10:00 — Product demo: 30m (recorded). Encourage questions in thread, not during demo.
  - 14:00 — Micro-assign: task with clear success criteria and <2hr scope.
- Day 3 (hands-on):
  - 09:30 — Pairing: buddy pairing session for the micro-assign.
  - 16:00 — Async doc drop: short doc describing code ownership areas + simple callouts.
- Day 4 (signal capture):
  - 11:00 — Checkpoint: manager 30m to capture signals (comfort with access, blockers). Use rubric below.
  - 15:00 — Team ritual participation (standup + 15m demo).
- Day 5 (celebrate + clear next steps):
  - 09:00 — Deliverable review: show micro-assign completed or with clear next actions.
  - 14:00 — 1-week retro: 20m manager+buddies (document in Confluence).

Manager checklist (quick actions):
- Send personal welcome note with "top 3 priorities in month 1".
- Book recurring 1:1 weekly for first 8 weeks.
- Identify a concrete small deliverable (2-4 hours) for week 1.
- Confirm buddy schedule and blockers owner.

Buddy checklist (practical):
- Share short keyboard/tooling cheat-sheet and helpful shortcuts.
- Reserve 2x30m pairing slots for week 1.
- Point to 3 essential docs and one demo video.
- Add new hire to relevant Slack channels and mute high-noise channels for first 48h.

Interview rubric subset (signals we want to preserve for hire->onboard transition):
- Cognitive fit: shows pattern recognition and debugging instincts (example prompt: "walk me through how you'd triage a deploy flake"). Score: 1-5 (note examples).
- Team comp: clear communication, can teach simple idea in 5 minutes. Score: 1-5.
- Ownership signal: shipping bias, small examples of follow-through. Score: 1-5.
- Practical ramp potential: learns new infra/tooling within 48-72h on a scaffolded task. Score: 1-5.
Notes: keep rubric examples short; include one line guidance for interviewers on evidence to collect (e.g., PR link, timeboxed project).

First-week success criteria (manager to verify):
- Access: all accounts with MFA working, verified by buddy.
- Context: new hire can summarize product in 3 sentences and name two stakeholders.
- Impact: micro-assign either merged or has an open PR with review notes.
- Wellbeing: new hire reports manageable cognitive load in 1-week retro.

Signal-based hiring plan pointers (for People Ops to track):
- If new hire cannot complete scaffolded 2hr task by Day 3, trigger "onboard-helper" flow (additional pairing + adjusted scope).
- If new hire reports >3 open blockers after Day 2, tag manager and people-ops for escalation.
- If team has repeated noise/over-scheduling infra, log "team sensory debt" and schedule a 1-hr retro.

Templates (copyable):
- Welcome email subject: "Welcome to Redwood — small plan for week one" (one paragraph + 3 bullets).
- Short manager script for Day1 AM: 1) why role matters, 2) one win for week1, 3) how to ask for help.
- Micro-assign template: title, goal, acceptance (what done looks like), estimate, owner, help contacts.

Edge cases & questions to resolve (notes to self):
- Contractor starts mid-sprint and needs limited infra access — define minimum viable access set. TODO: build template for contractor access (JIRA-SEC-210).
- Remote hires in APAC: timezone-sliced first-week schedule suggestions (suggested window: overlap 10:00-15:00).
- Neurodiversity accommodations: add opt-in preference form before Day 1.

Measurement & short-term metrics to track (people-ops):
- 1-week satisfaction NPS (2 questions).
- Time-to-first-PR (median).
- Percent of hires with done micro-assign in week1.

Open items (WIP):
- Create a small recorded "how we run standups" video (assigned to Jonah).
- Build the contractor access template (Priya).

Related links & tickets:
- Confluence onboarding templates: confluence.company.com/display/PO/Onboarding+Templates
- IT ticket (imaging): JIRA-IT-782
- Security baseline enrollment: JIRA-SEC-210
- Slack discussion: #people-ops-onboard (pinned threads)

Quick retrospective notes (from pilot cohort Nov 2025):
- Keep day1 team intro under 20 minutes; long slide decks overwhelm.
- New hires benefited from recorded product demo they could rewatch twice.
- Buddy availability is the most frequent blocker — formalize back-up buddy policy.

TODO (short):
- Convert micro-assign template into a short Linear/Jira story template.
- Add APAC timezone windows into the scheduling doc.

If you're using this doc: copy the templates, paste into the offer pack, and nudge the manager to commit to the first-week schedule 3 business days before start.

"Notes to self: this was written in one session — keep it pragmatic, not theatrical. Replace TODO tags with links before finalizing."
